summary: The Independent compares storylines in the first part of The Crown's sixth and final season, released on Netflix on 16 November 2023, with the real events they dramatise. It covers Diana's proposed role with Tony Blair's government, the Queen's attitude to Camilla, Dodi Fayed's engagement to Kelly Fisher, Diana's relationship with the paparazzi, and Dodi's ring and proposal. It also covers Mohamed al Fayed's role in the kiss photo and Prince William going missing at Balmoral. Some scenes are close to the record, while others, such as the proposal on the night of the crash and William's disappearance, are unconfirmed or invented.
one_line: A fact-check of The Crown season six part one, comparing its depictions of Diana, Dodi Fayed, Camilla and Prince William with real events.
key_facts: The final season of The Crown arrived on Netflix on Thursday 16 November 2023, with part two due on 14 December.
When season five arrived in 2022, there were calls for a "fictional explainer", which Netflix did not provide.
Part one of season six is set in summer 1997 and ends with the death of Diana and Dodi Fayed in a car crash in Paris.
Downing Street confirmed after Diana's death that she had visited Tony Blair at Chequers with her son weeks earlier, discussing a special role as an overseas "ambassador" for Britain.
Historian Robert Lacey says Queen Elizabeth was reluctant to accommodate Camilla and is said to have once called her "that wicked woman" to Charles's face, unlike in the show.
Elizabeth announced in 2005 that Camilla would be Princess Consort, but it was announced that Camilla would be queen seven months before Elizabeth's death.
Model Kelly Fisher, who met Dodi Fayed in July 1996, claimed to be engaged to him when he met Diana and filed a breach-of-contract lawsuit, which she dropped after his death.
Tina Brown, author of the 2007 book Diana Chronicles, claimed Diana often tipped off the press and "couldn't resist giving them the images they wanted".
Photographer Daniel Pirrie, who sold the kiss photo, told The Daily Mail in 2013 that Diana invited him and that he knew she wanted the kiss photo taken.
Biographer Tom Bower wrote in The Times that Mohamed al-Fayed gleefully showed him the photos and allegedly said he rapidly bought a yacht for his son's seduction of Diana.
In reality Dodi did not propose to Diana on the night of the crash, but CCTV shown at the 2007 inquest showed him buying a £11,600 engagement ring that afternoon.
A ring bearing the words "Dis-moi Oui" was recovered from Dodi's flat, alongside a receipt for a "bague de fiançaille".
It is not known whether William went missing at Balmoral, but in 2021 he recalled being told of his mother's death there and finding sanctuary at Crathie Kirk.
